title: Exploration
description: The front matter of an exploration's `exploration.md`: one question a person decides, with two or three divergent directions below it. With visuals (wireframes, screenshots, diagrams) it is a design or architecture exploration; with none, it is a decision card, named on a handoff note's Needs line. `aidd new exploration <folder>` writes it, and `aidd explore <folder>` renders its comparison page. The page records nothing: the owner role writes the person's pick and reason in the Spec's Design section, DESIGN.md, or an ADR. A technical spike is an exploration too: its timebox is the date it ends, and a person records its `outcome` and `evidence` here.

question.description: The question, in one sentence a person outside the team would understand.

owner.description: The aidd-team role that owns it and records the pick: the product designer for a UI question, the architect for an architecture one, or the role that asks.

timebox.description: Minutes or a cost, such as "45 minutes" or "2 USD"; when it runs out, the owner stops and presents. For a spike, the date it ends (YYYY-MM-DD): `aidd validate` warns when the date has passed and the status is still open with no `outcome`.

status.description: `open` until a person picks; `decided` once the owner has recorded the pick.

decided_round.description: The round the person picked in, set when the status becomes decided.

outcome.description: A spike's result, as a person records it when the timebox ends. The status is decided with it. An adopted spike that shapes the design also goes into an ADR or the Spec.

decision.description: `adopted`: the team uses what the spike tried. `rejected`: it does not. `inconclusive`: the timebox ended with no clear answer.

by.description: The person who decided, such as @lead. Never an agent.

evidence.description: What the outcome rests on: repository paths or URLs, such as a benchmark's results, a load-test report, or a throwaway branch.
